title: Review: Resident Evil might just be the best gaming adaptation yet
gist: Ars Technica's review argues director Zach Cregger's 2026 Resident Evil reboot, an original story set in the game universe rather than a direct adaptation, succeeds where the 2021 Welcome to Raccoon City reboot ($42M global box office against a $25M budget, critically panned) and a canceled 2022 Netflix series failed, crediting a single-protagonist structure, restrained humor, and body-horror execution.

insights.claim: The prior Resident Evil reboot, Welcome to Raccoon City (2021), was critically panned and grossed just $42 million globally against a $25 million budget, prompting the studio to scrap plans for a direct sequel.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Establishes the commercial bar the 2026 reboot needed to clear; a weak $42M global gross with panned reviews shows how quickly a major game-to-film franchise can stall commercially even with built-in IP recognition.
insights.locator: The first reboot, Welcome to Raccoon City (2021)

insights.claim: A 2022 Netflix Resident Evil series was canceled after a single season that was considered less-than-stellar, compounding the franchise's recent struggles across film and streaming formats prior to the 2026 reboot.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Shows repeated adaptation failure across two different media formats (film and streaming) for a major game IP, context for evaluating game-to-screen adaptation risk generally.
insights.locator: a 2022 Netflix series was also canceled

insights.claim: Director Zach Cregger, who had not seen the original Resident Evil films but was a fan of the games (especially Resident Evil 2), chose to tell an original story with original characters set in the game universe rather than a direct game adaptation, aiming for a single-protagonist journey without time jumps or narrative complexity.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Suggests a reusable playbook for successful game-to-film adaptation: prioritize universe fidelity and simple narrative structure over literal plot/character transcription from the source game.
insights.quote: no narrative acrobatics, time jumps, or disorienting chapter things
insights.locator: Cregger told the audience at CinemaCon earlier this year

insights.claim: Cregger's first cut of the film had significantly more humor, but test audiences felt it was too funny for a horror film, so he removed most of the jokes, which the reviewer says improved the movie.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: An example of test-screening-driven creative iteration materially changing tone balance in horror-comedy productions, relevant to how studios de-risk theatrical releases pre-launch.
insights.quote: A little bit of humor goes a long way in a horror movie, and there’s not a single joke I took out of this movie that I miss
insights.locator: Cregger told The Hollywood Reporter that his first cut

insights.claim: The film incorporates a third-person gameplay point-of-view shot style woven throughout to evoke the feeling of playing the game, without it becoming gimmicky, according to the reviewer.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Illustrates a specific cinematographic technique (game-camera POV) as a differentiator for appealing to both gamers and general audiences in video-game film adaptations.
insights.locator: Ditto for the third-person gameplay point of view

insights.claim: The reviewer calls the film 'terrific' and 'exceptionally well-made,' praising Austin Abrams' lead performance and arguing Cregger has finally cracked the long-standing challenge of adapting Resident Evil games to film and TV.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A strongly positive review from a major outlet could support stronger box-office performance than the 2021 reboot, relevant for entertainment-industry watchers tracking the film's commercial trajectory.
insights.quote: adapting the games to film and TV has proven to be a pretty formidable challenge… until now. Cregger has finally cracked the conundrum.
insights.locator: Fans expecting a more direct treatment
